newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gengold Sept qtr income edges up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Gengold Sept qtr income edges up slightly.

text.p: Gencor Ltd's gold division Gengold said on Monday that distributable income for the three months to end-September rose 1.8 percent to 57.4 million rand from 56.4 million in the preceding quarter.
Gold output was 10,104 kg, including production from Oryx, up six percent on the June quarter when output fell by 4.9 percent.
The overall yield declined by one percent to six grammes per tonne, after a 2.4 percent decline during the June quarter.
A total of 1.62 million tonnes of ore were milled, after a 2.5 percent decline in the previous quarter.

St Helena Gold Mines Ltd, which was threatened with closure two quarters ago, continued to power its way out of danger with bottom-line distributable income increasing by 60 percent to 6.6 million rand.
Winkelhaak Mines Ltd also advanced strongly, breaking even after the losses associated with its rationalisation in the June quarter.
Oryx, a unit of St Helena, whose future had been in the balance, resumed gold production during the period.
Gengold said it received an average gold price of 54,400 rand per kg in the September quarter, up 2.8 percent on the previous three months.
Total operating income for Beatrix Mines Ltd, Kinross Mines Ltd, Leslie Gold Mines Ltd, St Helena and Winkelhaak increased by 3.6 percent to 116 million rand.
But income after tax fell by 3.5 percent, reflecting substantial tax increases. Kinross had a particularly high tax bill, reflecting its return to profitibility.
Gold production cost increases were limited to 2.7 percent in spite of a higher wage bill.

"Implementation of the Gengold vision for operational restructuring is demonstrating that significant improvement to both safety management and productivity are practically achievable," said managing director Tom Dale.
"We expect the productivity improvements to become evident at the bottom-line during our 1997 financial year."
The company said the No.3 shaft expansion project at Beatrix remained on schedule and the metallurgical plant was commissioned last month.
Development and borehole drilling at Oryx are continuing to show in situ values which are better than those upon which a decision to refund Oryx was based, Gengold added.
